content.text:
Git refuses to stage anything that names an ignored file, even when it's named only to exclude it. When the git panel commits, it first runs `git add --all`, excluding `.suspense/commit-notes.json` so the notes don't end up in the commit. That file is now listed in `.gitignore`. So git printed "The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files" and exited with an error.

The staging itself still happened, so everything is staged right now, but the panel treated the error as a failure and never ran `git commit`. I reproduced this by running the same `git add` in this repo.

**Fix:** before staging, the panel now checks whether git already ignores the notes file. If it does, the file is left out anyway and isn't named. If it doesn't, as in a project without that `.gitignore` line, it's still excluded as before. The change is in `commit` in `src/git_panel.rs`.

**Test:** a new test commits in a scratch repository with and without the ignore rule. In both cases the commit succeeds and the notes file isn't in it. The git panel tests all pass. I didn't run the new test against the old code to watch it fail.

The app you have open is a release build from before the fix, so rebuild it with `cargo build --release` and try the commit again. Your changes and the four commit notes are still waiting.
